   1.  General Information

        Field Introduction

    Azadegan South Oil Field is situated in West Karoun province on a large long-axis anticline
    with N-S trending with approximate dimensions about 20 km width and 60 km length near
    to Iran-Iraq border, to the east of Yaran Oil Field.

   The trap area of the south Azadegan is limited to 43.2x17.2 km. The Azadegan Oil field was
    discovered in 1999, when Well AZN-1 was drilled vertically down to the Cretaceous
    Fahliyan Formation with total depth of 4,643m. The results of this well, revealed the reservoir
     characteristics of the field. Following to the result of the well no. AZN-1, another 5
    exploration wells was drilled in different parts of this huge field down to Fahliyan Formation.
    In the later stage the well No.10 assumed as exploration well for evaluation of deeper
    formations. This well was drilled in 2008, down to the depth of 5340m (Neyriz Fm.), mainly
    to evaluate the Jurassic formations.

    Based on the exploration wells results, carbonate reservoir of Sarvak Formation is broadly
    developed in Azadegan Field. This formation was penetrated in all of seven exploration wells
    (AZN-1, AZN-2, AZN-3, AZN-4, AZN-5, AZN-6 and AZN-10). Clastic oil-bearing zones
    of Kazhdumi Formation developed in main anticline of Azadegan Field, extending from
    north to center of South Azadegan. The Clastic oil-bearing zones of Gadvan Formation
    developed only in crest area and south parts of South Azadegan Filed, which was discovered
   by AZN-1 in crest and AZN-4 in south parts. The carbonates of Fahliyan Formation also
    developed in Azadegan field, but the oil reservoir of this formation developed in South part
    of South Azadegan.

   The Azadegan Field is an elongated anticline, trending in N-S direction, belonging to
    "Arabian Trend".

   The stratigraphy sequence of the field includes AghaJari, Gachsaran, Fahliyan, Pabdeh,
    Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan Formations, from
    top to bottom. This sequence in well no AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well of the
     field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus and Neyriz formations.

   The Dominant lithofacies of Sarvak Formation are Rudist-bearing packstone and partially
    grainstone, which contains abundant bioclasts. Some other facies like matrix-dominated
    wackestone and mudstone are also found.

   The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province and is Approximately Located
    80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest of The
  YADAVARAN  Field and  in The West  of JUFEYR  Field. The Average Monthly
    Temperature is 45ºc in summer, and Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature
     is -4.4ºc in winter. Maximum Rainfall is 78 mm in February, Winter Season.

         Reservoir Information
     Key Reservoir Descriptions

      Fahliyan Formation: This carbonate to argillaceous carbonate Formation is limited by
      overlying thick argillaceous successions in the upper part (eaquivalent to the Iraqi
      Ratawi Formation) and the main part consists of different bioclastic limestones with
     some layers of shale and argillaceous facies that can be assumed equivalent with Iraqi
    Yamama Formation. However, in South Azadegan wells 1, 2 and 5 the Fahliyan
      Formation is characterized by fossiliferous limestone beds and interbedded shales. It
      should be noted that most of Majnoon wells penetrated into the Sarvak and Fahliyan
      carbonates as one of the main reservoir targets.

        AZNS-040 Well History

     The AZNS-040 well was drilled from 26-Mar-2014 to 10-May-2014 by CNPCI to total
      depth 1493m and suspended. Drilling and well suspend sequences are describe in the
      following.
     26” Hole Section Summary

      This section was drilled from 15 to 153 m using one rock bit (26" Simth, Type:
    MSDGH, IADC 135) and bentonite mud w/ 65.5-71.8 pcf weight. Performed ream
     and back ream prior to each connection. When TD was reached, wiper trip and
    CBU to clean the hole were done with good condition. Spotted Hi-Vis pill at
      bottom, dropped single shot to take a survey that resulted in 0.2° at 150 m. 20ʺ
    CSG (K-55, 117 ppf, Big Omega) was run to 152.5 m and cemented in place by
       stinger with 346 bbls cement class G, 117 pcf. 50 bbls slurry returned to surface.
     N/U 20 3⁄4ʺ CHH 3K on 20ʺ CGS supported by a base plate and performed
      pressure test by 400 psi, 15min. N/U 20 3⁄4ʺ BOP 3K and performed pressure test.
     17 1⁄2ʺ milled tooth bit was RIH, tagged TOC at 150.5 m, 20ʺ CGS pressure tested
      with 1650 psi /15min, then D/O cement & shoe.
      Total Duration for this section was 4 days and 2 hrs. until new formation of next
      section was started to drill.

      17-1/2” Hole Section Summary

      Drilled 17 1⁄2" hole section from 153m to 1493m, MW: 71.8-85.5pcf NaCl-KCl polymer
    Mud &Saturated NaCl Polymer Mud. LOT@156m with 80psi, MW: 71.1pcf, EMD:
      93.64 pcf. Took survey and wiper trip every 200m to ensure good well track and hole
      condition, try to control viscosity and water loss of mud as program, due to claystone &
     gypsum exist in the interval. From the depth of 1159m to 1385m, we meet very low ROP
     (min-ROP is 0.1 m/h). total used 5pcs of bits (1 used rock bit, 3 used PDC bits and 1
     new PDC bit) when during drilling 17-1/2" hole. total footage 1340m, actual drilling
      time 687.3Hrs, ROP: 1.95 m/h.

      Performed condition hole before run wireline logging (Items: GR, CDR, CALI). After
      logging performed 1 more time hole condition prior to run casing, Spotted high viscosity
    mud pill at bottom of the hole. Ran 13 3/8" CSG (68ppf-N80-BTC) to 1492m (casing
      shoe0.

      Performed cementing job: Cement track pumped 25m3 spacer (1.05sg) with FR 317gpm,
     SPP 200-478psi, dropped BTM plug, pumped 2m3 of spacer(1.05sg), follow by 147.0m3
      of lead slurry(average 1.45sg, Max 1.51sg, Min 1.45sg ) with FR 528gpm, SPP 1015-
      345psi, pumped 48m3 tail slurry (average 1.85sg, Max 1.89sg, Min 1.83sg) with FR
     528gpm SPP345-0psi. Released top plug, pumped 2m3 of tail slurry (average 1.00sg)
      with FR 264gpm, SPP 0psi. Pumped 1m3 of fresh water with FR 264gpm, SPP 0psi.
      Switch to rig pump, displace mud (1.37sg) with FR 740-264gpm, SPP 350-480psi,
     bumped plug pressure from 732psi to 1083psi. Bleed pressure. 56m3 neat cement slurry
      returned to surface.

       Install 20-3/4"*3K-13-5/8"*5K CHS. P/T of seal of flange connection with 1500psi/
      10min, OK. N/U 13-5/8"*10K BOP single ram.

     RIH from surface to 285m with 5"DP to put CMT plug f/50-150 meter below the WH.
     P/T 13- 3/8" casing with 3000psi/15min, MW 85.49pcf, OK. POOH from 285m to
     200m. Pumped 4m3 1.37SG H-Vis mud. POOH from 200m to 150m. Pump 1.0 m3
      spacer (fresh water), Pump 8m3 of lead slurry (average 1.85sg), POOH from 150m to
       surface. WOC, While L/D 5"DPS.

     Tagged top of cement plug @55m with 3 Ton.

        AZNS-040 Re-Entry Well Program Outline

     AZNS-40 well, was planned to be drilled as Horizontal well in Sarvak formation
     on Pad-50. The well was drilled by CNPCI to total depth 1493m in Gachsaran
      formation as 17-1/2” hole section, 13-3/8” CSG ran and cemented to surface and
      well has been suspended by CMT plug.

     As the Previous exploration/delineation drilling in Azadegan oilfield has proved
      presence of a very prolific hydrocarbon bearing sedimentary column, particularly
      within the Cretaceous sequences. The Fahliyan Formation was divided into 6
      zones, named as Fahliyan top, Fah-1, Fah-2, Fah-3, Fah-4 and Fah-5.

     The objective of Re-Entry this well is to De-suspend the well, vertical drilling 12-
      1/4″ & 8-1/2″ hole section to new well target in Fahliyan reservoir (Well target
     has been changed from Sarvak horizontal well to Fahliyan vertical well), run
      9-5/8” CSG and 7” Liner, perforate 7” Liner in Fahliyan formation and complete
      the well as Fahliyan vertical oil producer well.

     The AZNS-040 Re-Entry sequences summarize as follow:

     De-Suspend the Well:

      Monitor wellhead pressure and make sure about wellhead integrity. Remove wellhead
      cover, N/U BOPs. P/U & M/U 12-1/4” D/Out BHA, RIH to top of CMT plug @ 55m,
     D/Out CMT plug f/ 55-100m with water, RIH to top of 13-3/8” CSG Float collar, D/Out
      shoe track to 3m above shoe with water, displace well with 75 pcf Salt Saturated/Polymer
     mud, perform 13-3/8” CIT, D/Out shoe track to 1493m.
      Note: if wellhead pressure is not Zero after Bleed off, Contractor shall inform client.
     Remedial plan to be prepared in advance by operators and will be followed after client’s
      confirmation.

     12-¼" Hole Section:

       Drill 12-1/4” vertical hole section f/ 1493m to 3986m through Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi,
      Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan formations with 75-85
      pcf Salt Saturated KCL/Glycol/Polymer mud. Then Full Suite/CDR/GR Logs will be
       run. The 9-5/8” Casing will be set at  3986m and it will be cemented in one stage as
      primary cementing up to surface. N/U13-5/8”, 5K x 11”, 10K THS and then N/U 13-
       5/8”, 10K BOPs. RIH with D/Out BHA to TOC, D/Out to 7m above shoe, perform 9-
      5/8” CIT. Run D/Out 9-5/8” Cement quality log. RIH with 8-1/2” PDC Bit BHA to 7m
     above shoe, D/Out shoe track to 3986m while displace well with 100 pcf Salt Saturated
     Kcl/Polymer/CaCo3 mud.

     8-½" Hole Section:

     The 8-½" hole section will be drilled vertically from 3986m to 4200m in Fahliyan
      formation with 100-106 pcf  Salt Saturated Kcl/Polymer/CaCo3 mud. Then  Full
     Suite/CDR/GR Logs will be carried out over 8-½" open hole section to evaluate Fahliyan
       reservoir. The 7” Liner will be run and set at ± 4200m and it will be cemented in one
      stage as primary cementing up to  7 Stands Wet above Liner Lap. Clean out to 7” L.Lap
     and inside 7” liner to LDC. Perform 7” Liner CIT, L.Lap positive and negative tests and
      run 7” Liner Cement quality Log. Displace 7” Liner volume with CaBr2 perforation
       fluid, perform 7” Liner perforation, run CCL/GR log to confirm perforated interval. RIH
      with 5-7/8” Bit to top of perforation while scrap 7” production PKR setting depth,
      displace well volume with CaBr2 completion  fluid. Run 4-1/2" *  3-1/2", 10K
      Completion string. N/D BOP, N/U XMT. Perform well Pre-Acid clean up, Acid-Wash,
      Post-Acid clean up and well performance test operations. Secure the well and release the
     Rig

      2.  Geological Information

            Structural Geology

       The Azadegan oil field is located at 80km west of Ahwaz is an elongated anticline,
         trending in N-S direction, belongs to Arabian Trend which is different from
        “Zagros Trend”. There is no outcrop for Azadegan structure and it was detected
        by 2D seismic interpretation. The Previous exploration/delineation drilling in
        Azadegan oil field has proved presence of a very prolific hydrocarbon bearing
         sedimentary column, particularly within the Cretaceous sequences. Fahliyan
        Formation is one of the important hydrocarbon reservoirs in the southern part of
        Azadegan  field, which has been developed  in  recent  years. The Fahliyan
        Formation was divided into 6 zones, named as Fahliyan top, Fah-1, Fah-2, Fah-3,
        Fah-4 and Fah-5.

                Figure 2-1: Distribution of Fahliyan wells in South Azadegan Oilfield on Top of Fah-1 Zone

          Formation Description

       The stratigraphy sequence of this field includes Aghajari, Gachsaran, Asmari,
        Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan
         formations. This sequence in well no. AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well
         of the field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus and Neyriz
         formations.

                             Figure 2-2: Stratigraphy Column of South Azadegan Oilfield

       The AZN-040 Re-Entry well is carried out inside of Gachsaran to Fahliyan
         Formations, a  brief  stratigraphic  description  of  these formations  in South
        Azadegan field has been described as follows:

             Gachsaran Formation

                                                                                  Page 34 of 240

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
            Azadegan Oil Field Development

                  Geological Forecast and Drilling Recommendations for well
Contract No:                   AZN-040 Workover (Deep)                                                                                           Page 35 of 240
053-073-9125         Project     P/T      Zone    Departman    Discipline     Doc.      Sequence      Rev.
               SAC     P      IIF40    DR      DE    PRG      0027      00

         This formation begins with white, glassy, soft, medium, hard anhydrite and off
         white, light gray to gray, soft to medium hard, dolomitic limestone. Comprises of
         anhydrite interbedded with gray marl and red marl, salt beds of variable thickness
        and some thin limestone beds. This formation in type section not divided to other
        member. The Anhydrite is white off white, milky, soft, and partly crystalline to
          crystalline, medium hard to hard. The Gray marl is gray to light gray, soft. The
       Red marl is red brown to brown, soft, sticky. The Limestone is gray to light gray,
         buff to buff gray, hard, and slightly dolomitic.

             Asmari Formation
       The Asmari Formation in Azadegan Field developed a massive sandstone interval,
         with a few thin argillaceous limestones in the upper sections. Sandstone are clear,
          fine to medium-sorted, and poorly consolidated. On the other hand, the lower
         sections consist of intercalation of sandy, chalky, slightly dolomitic high-energy
         limestone with sandstone layers.

             Pabdeh Formation
        Pabdeh Formation is divided into two parts in the Azadegan field. The upper part
           is made of grey to dark- brown argillaceous limestone and marl. Planktonic fauna
         dates that this part was deposited in Oligocene. The lower part is composed of
         dark-brown, slightly argillaceous limestone. Pelagic fauna, mostly Globigerina
        and Globorotalia, indicates that this part was formed during late Paleocene to late
        Eocene in age. It seems that no early Paleocene formation exists in the Azadegan
          area.

             Gurpi Formation
         This formation consists of three main units: a) Upper Gurpi Member, b) Tarbour
       Tongue and c) Lower Gurpi Member.

       Upper Gurpi Member
         This member begins with light gray, gray, off white, soft to medium, sticky
         argillaceous limestone. The Upper Gurpi Member is mostly consisting of gray buff
          to gray with of trace partly buff gray, dark gray, medium hard to hard argillaceous,
         high argillaceous graded to marl argillaceous limestone interbedded with anhydrite
        marl and chalky limestone beds. The anhydritic marl is light gray to gray, soft,
          sticky, graded to high argillaceous calcareous. The chalky limestone is light gray
          to buff gray, medium hard to soft, chalky. II, a slightly argillaceous.

       Tarbur Tongue
         In the western Abadan Plain about 50 meters thick chalky limestone was
         encountered in the middle part of the Gurpi Formation, which contains abundant

                                                                                  Page 35 of 240

         fragments of bioclasts, suggesting very shallow depositional environment. This
          interval is equivalnt to the Tarbur Formation with reservoir quality in other
          regions.

       Lower Gurpi Member
         This Member begins with off white, cream, soft to medium hard argillaceous
         limestone and light gray to gray, soft, sticky marl. The Member consisting of dark
         gray to gray, light gray, soft to medium hard argillaceous limestone and light cream
        and soft. II, A. chalky limestone beds.

             Ilam Formation
         This formation is mostly consisting of limestone interbedded with shale and clay
         stone beds. The Limestone is cream, buff to buff gray, light brown, soft to medium
         hard, chalky, II, A, oil stained Partly slightly argillaceous. The Shale is green gray
          to light green gray, mostly brown gray, medium hard, pyritic, slightly calcareous.
       The Claystone is green gray to light green gray and soft, slightly calcareous.

             Laffan Formation
       The Laffan Formation is mostly consists of greenish-grey pyritic shale layer with
         ostracods fauna interbedded with Claystone beds  that capping  the Sarvak
         Formation.

             Sarvak Formation
       The Sarvak Formation developed a carbonate unit, which was gradually overlying
         the Kazhdumi Formation, and  it is abruptly terminated by an erosion phase,
        covered by a various late Cretaceous sediment. The lithology of Sarvak consists
         of the dark grey fine grained nodular argillaceous limestone interbedded with thin
         marls in the bottom. The Limestone graded upward into a white-to-buff massive
         chalky limestone with siliceous nodules; developed a very massive tan-to-brown
         limestone containing abundant rudist debris in the middle part. In the upper part is
       made up of rubbly limestone with red staining and leached zones of breccia and
         the top of Sarvak Formation is very ferruginous. For the layering scheme of the
          reservoir section, sequence stratigraphic concept was applied to the Azadegan
          wells. Judging from the characteristics of gamma ray and other wireline logs,
          relative sea- level change during the deposition of the reservoir sections were
          interpreted in terms of sequence stratigraphic context. Based upon the sea-level
        change inferred, the sections were interpreted as vertical accumulation of a number
         of zones, each of which  is geologically termed as a depositional sequence,
          implicitly representing a genetically related body of sedimentary sequence. The
         formation was divided totally into thirteen zones by interpreting.

            Kazhdumi Formation
         This formation is start with dark brown to dark green gray, medium hard to hard,
          soft to medium, high Bituminous, calcareous shale interbedded with argillaceous
         limestone, sandy claystone, claystone, marl, sandy limestone, limestone beds. the
        middle part developed light-grey, micritic to chalky limestone, the low part, is
        around 40-60m in thichness clean channel sands interbeded with  argillaceous
         sands with streaks of shale.

             Dariyan Formation
         In the Azadegan Field, the average thickness of the Dariyan Formation is 183.5 m;
            its greatest thickness is 197.5 m in well AZN-1. This formation overlies the
       Gadvan Formation conformably and is overlain disconformably by the Kazhdumi
         Formation. Dariyan Formation  starts with white to white cream grey clean
         limestone type I/II, I. Base of Dariyan Formation appears grey, green pyritic shale
         interbedded with argillaceous limestone. This zone called transition zone and
         thickness is 16m. after last grey limestone indicates of Gadvan Formation.

            Gadvan Formation
         In this formation a variety of lithological rock types such as carbonates, rich
         organic shales and sandstones were deposited in various environments. The lower
          part of the Gadvan Formation is composed of low- energy, but not very deep,
          micritic, often argillaceous limestone with echinoids and algal fragments. Two
         sandstone units were defined in the Gadvan Formation  lateral changes and
         especially discontinuity of the sandstone layers which are consist of fine clastics
          (shales and siltstones) may be expected The Gadvan formation divided to three
          part:

       Upper Gadvan
       The upper part appears with occurrence of terrigenous rock. The lithology is
        composed of grey claystone and some shale.

       Khalij Member
       The Khalij member appear with pure limestone, cream, light brown and in some
          intervals oil stain.

       Lower Gadvan
       The lower part consisting of alternating of marl, argillaceous limestone, limestone,
         claystone, sandy claystone and sandstone beds. The Marl is green gray, soft, sticky,
          slightly calcareous. The Argillaceous Limestone is gray white gray medium hard

          to soft, partly pyritic. The Limestone is white, white to light gray, hard. The
         Claystone is light gray, soft, sticky. The Sandy Claystone is light gray, soft, sticky,
          fine sand grained. The Sandstone is brown to gray, partly white buff, gray, friable,
          sorted, sub rounded, medium quartz grained, partly calcareous. This sandstone
        which occur in Zone-3 and Zone-5 are the reservoir of this formation and in this
          part is equivalent with Kushk member.

             Fahliyan Formation
         This formation is start with light gray, light green gray, soft Limestone interbedded
         with green gray, soft, sticky Marl, green gray, light gray, soft, Argillaceous
        Limestone and dark green gray, soft, sticky Clay stone beds. This formation at
         continue is consisting of buff white light gray, light brown, brown, medium hard,
         hard, densely, slightly argillaceous limestone and off white, white gray, medium
         hard chalky limestone beds.

          Logging and Testing Program
        Logging Program

        Well AZNS-040 will undergo wireline logging operation in all required intervals.
         Since this well logging plan is targeted to evaluate the hydrocarbon potential, the
           full suite Logs should be run in 12-¼” and 8-½" open hole to collect reservoir and
         required data.
        Logging is limited to GR/CDR logs in 12-¼” and 8-½" open holes and CAST log
          in 9-5/8” casing and 7” Liner that must be carried out by wire line.

    3.  Nearby Wells

     The well AZNS-040 is located in Pad#50 and as per well geology program and pad
       location proximity wells the nearby wells are AZNS-045, AZNS-127, AZN-010 and
     AZNS-017.

        Nearby Wells Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned

       Drilling challenges and lesson learned for well AZNS-040 are extracted from DDR and
    EOWR of nearby wells.
      Furthermore, based on NBW study, the well AZNS-017 is a Kazhdumi Horizontal well
     and it’s drilling sequences are different from typical Fahliyan well in South Azadegan
        oilfield, therefore all drilling challenges and lesson learned have been correlated to
       typical Fahliyan well sequences.

      Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 26” Hole Section

      Generally, 26” hole section is first step of drilling sequence in AZNS oilfield and it will
      be drill through Aghajari formation.
      This hole section main issue while drilling including Tight hole, Bit/stabilizer balling
     and hole deviation control.
     The best practice to drill this hole section is to commence drilling with low parameters
     and high viscous spud mud for first drilled stand in order to prevent washout around well
       location/cellar area, then increase drilling parameters to maximum gradually.
      In order to prevent Bit/Stabilizer balling, flow rate and mud properties must be in range.
      For preventing hole  deviation, use  stabilized BHA and  drilling with  controlled
      parameters, if hole deviate from vertical, try to decrease hole inclination by reaming and
      varying drilling parameters such as decrease WOB and increase RPM.
      Furthermore, reamer trip is essential to make hole as smooth as possible prior to run
       casing.
      In well AZNS-040 this section already drilled to 153m with 65-71 pcf Mw and 20” CSG
      has been run to TD and cemented to surface without any problem.
     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
         1. Bit balling in well AZNS-045 with 65 pcf Bentonite mud.
         2. Noticeable cement losses while cementing 18-5/8” CSG with 115 pcf Sw in well
          AZNS-017.

      Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 17-1/2” Hole Section

      For typical Fahliyan vertical well in area II, this hole section drill through Gachsaran
      formation which is not high pressure in this zone.
     Based on NBW study and formation description, the main drilling issues in 17-1/2” hole
      are tight hole, calcium ion contamination, hole deviation from vertical and CMT loss
      while CSG cementing.
     While drilling through Gachsaran formation, drilling fluid must be salt saturated and Mw
     must be adjust with hole condition and in case of any indication of abnormality while
       drilling/tripping/reaming such as Hi-Trq, abnormal drag, tight hole, increase in calcium
      ion value, etc, the Mw should increase in 1 pcf increment to overcome drilling issues
     and prevent induced losses, also mud should be inhibited with Kcl or any caly inhibition
       additive to achieve better hole condition.
      For good hole condition and reasonable ROP, mud properties must be in range and flow
       rate must be as maximum acceptable rate especially while drilling with PDC Bit to obtain
      planned HIS.
     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
         1. Frequent Bit and Stabilizer balling in GS formation with 67-86 pcf KCL/Polymer
        mud due to bad mud properties in well AZNS-045.
         2. Drilling fluid contamination with Ca++ in Gachsaran formation in well AZNS-045.
         3. String stuck in GS formation in well AZNS-045 while back reaming due to bad
            hole condition with 84 pcf KCL/Polymer mud.
         4. Observed back flow after cementing 13-3/8” CSG in well AZNS-045, fix problem
              after several step apply pressure in well and hold.
         5. Frequent tight hole and reaming due to low Mw with respect to hole condition in
           base of Aghajari formation in well AZNS-017.
         6. Bit and Stabilizer balling due to low Mw and improper Mud properties in well
          AZNS-017. Mud must be inhibited to drill clay formation.
         7. Washing down 13-3/8” Casing and set casing off bottom (5.5m) due to bad hole
            condition in well AZNS-017.
         8. Bill balling in well AZNS-127 in base of GS formation.
         9. Frequent tight hole and string washout in GS formation in AZN-010 while drilling
           with 74-90 pcf Mw.

      Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 12-1/4” Hole Section

               SAC     P      IIF40    DR      DE    PRG      0027      00

      For typical Fahliyan vertical well in area II, this hole section drilling starts from Asmari
      formation and will be finish to top of Fahliyan formation and pass through Sarvak,
     Kazhdumi and Gadvan reservoirs which contain H2S and Co2.
     The 9-5/8” Production Casing will be set in top of Fahliyan to isolate high pressure
      Fahliyan formation from other formation.
     The key point while drilling this hole section is to adjust proper Mw with respect to hole
      condition in order to prevent hole problems such as tight hole, wellbore stability
      problem, string stuck and induced losses.
      Also, inhibited drilling fluid system must be used to drill this hole section due to presence
      of different kind of formation, the normal inhibition additives such as PHPA, KCL,
      Glycol must be used in system with regard to formation being drilled and mud properties
     must be controlled as per program.
      Consider H2S and Co2 effect on mud while drilling through SV, KZ, GD formation and
       try to keep PH in range.
     As per NBW study, this section is challenging hole section of typical Fahliyan vertical
      well profile and tight hole, wellbore stability problems, mud contamination, string
      washout and string stuck have been recorded frequently in this hole section.
     The best practice to drill safely is to start drilling with salt saturated polymer mud and
      change add Kcl into mud before top of Pabdeh and control Mw as low as possible while
       drilling AS/Pabdeh formations and continue drilling while increase Mw in 1 pcf
      increment with CaCo3 if observed any abnormal sign while drilling/tripping such as Hi-
      Trq, abnormal drag, increase in calcium ion value, etc. Consider losses while drilling
      through SV formation.
      Furthermore, while drilling through Sarvak and Kazhdumi formations, mud inhibition
     must be in range (Glycol/Kcl). In case of any losses in AS, PD and SV formations tried
       to cure same with proper LCM while keep Mw as low as possible.
      Also, due to drilling through different H2S bearing formation in this section, consider
    H2S safety requirement.
     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
         1. Frequent Tight hole in GU formation (Lower) in well AZNS-045 due to low Mw
          and improper mud inhibition.
         2. Drilling through AS/PD/GU with 2-6 BPH losses with 75-84 pcf Mw in well
          AZNS-045. Drilling to section TD with 0-2 BPH losses with 84-87.5 pcf Mw.
         3. Differential String stuck in KZ formation in well AZNS-045, free same with HCL
           Acid, cut Mw from 87.5 pcf to 81 pcf.

5.  Sequence of Operation

     Rig Move
  Hold pre-move meeting on location. Discuss contingency plans for:
  Safe arrangements for R/U and R/D.
  Safe standby areas for Rig.
  In case move have to be suspended.
  Loss of trucks in case of repair.
 Moving at night.
  Hold pre-move safety meeting. Ensure everyone understands individual responsibilities:
  Commence rigging down. The ordering of trucks will be done by rig manager.
  Commence Rig move to AZNS-40, PAD NO. 50

  Position Rig for optimal operations.
 Mud tanks should be empty during move. Fill water tanks and keep as full as possible

  Rig up on cellar
  Final rig up and commence operational procedure for (AZNS-40)
  Before leaving previous location, all equipment should be checked.
  Test all manifold and surface safety valves

     Pre-spud
   Certificate
   1. All Rig equipment is on location, properly rigged up and function-tested. Check availability
     and content of Rig equipment inspection & maintenance records according to Client and
    API standards.

   Safety Device
   1. Test draw-works crown block saver and record results on daily drilling report; test derrick
    man escape device (Geronimo line) and record time required for test weight on daily
      drilling report; test rig intercom system, especially for Driller-Derrick Man and Driller-
    Mud Logger communication link.
   2. Check that all rig safety equipment, e.g., fire extinguishers, eye-wash stations etc., is
      installed at the proper locations as per rig layout diagrams.
   3. Verify that substructure is level and foundation adequate to support drilling unit during
     whole well period and that mast is centered above rotary table.

   4. Ensure rig alignment with Top Drive System. Make sure rig tongs and rig floor hoisting
     equipment are adequate for handling 8-1/2″ drill collars. Make sure that mechanical tong
      torque gauges for drill pipe/drill collar are properly functioning and have been calibrated;
      re-calibrated as required.

  Rig Equipment
   1. Verify that the De-suspension phase and 12-1/4” phase equipment is available in Rig site.
   2. 12-1/4” Tri-cone Bit is ready to be picked up, all nozzles installed and 12-1/4″ Bit breaker
      are on the rig floor.
   3. Make sure single-shot or multi-shot survey tools available for vertical section survey.
   4. Make sure all solids control equipment are correctly installed and have been function-tested
     with charging pressure gauges in place where applicable. Make sure adequate screen
      inventory for the shale shakers is available in the sizes required for the well. Make sure
     water tanks are completely filled and transfer lines from water tanks to mud system are
     hooked up. Make sure all mud materials and chemicals required to drill 12-1/4″ hole section
       is on location, in sound condition and suitably stored. Make sure that De-suspension fluid
     and kill mud has been made in sufficient volume.
   5. Make sure that all mud pumps have been fitted with new consumable parts: liners, pistons,
      valves, seats etc. Make sure that pulsation dampeners are charged with Nitrogen to the
     proper pre-charge pressure, 30% of expected standpipe pressure during drilling of the 12-
     1/4” hole section; check if sufficient Nitrogen bottles are available on location to adjust
      pulsation dampener pre-charge pressure as required. Make sure that mud pump pop-off
      valves are set at the proper pressure for the liner sizes installed and that the mud discharge
      lines from the pop-off valves to the mud tanks are properly secured. Check that all high-
      pressure hoses are properly secured with safety chains. P/T should be done to high-pressure
      surface line of circulating system.

  Wellhead & BOP
   1. 20-3/4” 3K CHH and 20-3/4”, 3K x 13-5/8”, 5K CHS. Have cover on CHS.
   2. Record well head and annulus pressure under Client supervision.
   3. Overall check of well head components and function same, verify all are in good working
      order under Cliet supervision.
   4. 13-5/8”, 10K BOPs and related well control equipment must be ready in Rig site and
      pressure tested on test stump and ready for N/U on well head.
   5. Make sure proper Cup tester, plug tester and wear bushing are available in Rig site.

  Others
   1. Make sure that adequate supply of tools and equipment for De-suspension and drilling 12-
     1/4” hole section is available.

Sequence of Operation
   1. Record well head and annulus pressure. If any pressure, bleed off and make sure pressure is zero and
      does not charge again.

NOTE:
    If there is any pressure after bleed off, call town for instruction.

   2. Remove well head cover. Visually check well head, 13-3/8” CSG slip and CHS ring groove,
    make sure all are in good working order.
   3. N/U 13-5/8”, 10M BOPs (13-5/8”, 5M Annular preventer, 13-5/8, 10M Double Ram preventer
      including Pipe Ram and Shear/Blind Ram & 13-5/8”, 10M Single Pipe Ram preventer) and
      related lines. N/U bell nipple and flow line.

NOTE:
   N/U all BOPs component on BOP stump as Rig-less, test same and be ready for final N/U
      on WH.

   4. Function test Accumulator unit. Function & P/T BOPs and related lines as per NIOC standard.
   5. Perform WH pressure integrity test by Cup tester.

NOTE:
   Make sure proper Cup test is available at well site.
   Limit P/T to 80% of WH RWP.

   6. P/U and M/U 12-1/4” TCI Bit (Bit#1, 517 w/ 3x15/32” Jet Nozzles) and D/Out BHA (Including
     Junk sub), RIH to tag top of Cement plug @ 55m.
   7. D/Out Cement plug f/ 55-100m with water while sweeping well with Hi-vis pill intermittently
     and dump remained fluid in the well.

D/Out Parameters:
    Flow Rate: 400-500 GPM
    RPM: 60
    WOB: 5-20 Klbs

NOTE:
    Start D/Out CMT plug with 5 Jts 8-1/2” DC and add BHA components as D/Out progress.
    Be careful for probable trapped pressure below CMT plug.

   8. Cont’ RIH joint by joint to tag top of 13-3/8” Float Collar (Cementing Plugs) @ 1468m.
   9. D/Out Plugs, F.Collar and CMT to 3m above 13-3/8” Shoe @ 1489m. Work on junk sub.

        D/Out Parameters:

NOTE:
    Function test floating equipment.
    Casing shoe should be adjusted in such a way to have minimum Rat hole and enough stick
       up (1.5m) on rig floor.

    Fill casing with Non-LCM fresh mud every 10 joints (or every jt with F/U tool).
    Do not forget to change Top Ram before/after CSG running.

    Cementing
   16. R/U cementing head with related lines (DSV shall witness the loading of plugs). P/T the lines
      to 4000 psi for 15 minutes. Pump mud as 1.2 casing annulus volume.
   17. Cement casing as per program. Displace with mud. Bump the plug with 500 psi over the final
      circulating pressure or maximum 3000 psi pressure. Bleed off pressure, check for back flow.
    R/D cementing head.

NOTE:
   Make sure that the cement head is capable of holding pressure while displacing and testing
      cement (Visually).
   Any minor adjustment for Cementing program regarding the corrected depth will be done in
      due time.
   Rig pump efficiency should be check in trip-tank before cement job.
   Closely monitor cementing pressure. Record and report the final pressure before bump the
       plug.
   Cementing Truck must be equipped with DAS to record job.
    If cement returns to surface and observe bumping with 3000 psi while displacing cement
        slurry, hold pressure for 15 minutes and assume bumping pressure as Casing integrity test and
       note in DDR.
    If bumping was not observed, CIT must be performed after D/Out CMT to 7m above shoe.

     performance test as per completion program.
   35. Secure the well and release the Rig.

Discussion

12-1/4" Interval will be drilled through formations of Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak,
Kazhdumi, Darian and Gadvan. Salt/ KCl/ Glycol/ Sulfonated Asphalt/ CaCo3/Polymer Mud is
designed for drilling this section. Shoe of 9⅝" casing will be set at 3986m in top of Fahliyan. Different
rates of downhole losses, from seepage to complete, may be experienced through this section. Tight
hole leading to pipe stuck is the other risk of drilling here.
Based on the lithology to be drilled in 12-1/4” hole section, it is necessary to utilize shale inhibitors
in active system in case of need. The primary shale inhibitor in the system is Potassium ion for cation
exchange in the clays structure, to reduce their capacity of hydration and swelling. This will be
provided by KCl concentration of ≥15 ppb, but to be added only 100 m prior to reach Pabdeh
formation (due to probable losses in Asmari formation).
Inhibition of hydratable lithology, especially in Kazhdumi, is going to be provided by existence of 15
pbb KCl in mud system and minimum 2-3% by volume of High Temperature Cloud Point Glycol. it
is recommended to have initial sufficient concentration of KCl (along with formulated 2-3% Glycol)
in the system to commence a safe and smooth drilling through Kazhdumi formation, Since KCl of the
mud is a disturbing factor for the quality of the Gamma log, the KCl will be allowed to be depleted
and not maintained in the course of onward drilling, so that the concentration of disturbing potassium
ion drops down. Glycol might play the role of primary shale inhibitor for the intervals exposed to
low-KCl mud.
To minimize the risk of polymer fermentation whilst drilling, Oxygen Scavenger S is formulated at
concentration of 0.3 ppb while having routine daily treatment as well. A very commonly used type of
oxygen scavenger is a Sodium Sulphate-based product (If required). It reacts with and eliminates

                                                                              Page 99 of 240

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 100 of 240 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

dissolved oxygen as a factor of increasing fermentation rate of natural-sourced polymers and also as
a potential source of metal corrosion in mud systems.
KCl will be allowed to be depleted gradually in the course of drilling. It will be maintained only if
situation dictates. Use of 3-4 ppb Sulfonated Asphalt while drilling through Laffan formation may be
helpful against the threat of Laffan Shale hydration in case of hole dictation. This will also improve
the quality of wellbore when we are close to running casing.
NaCl (72 ppb) should be solved in base water to get 72.5 pcf brine. Starch HT at 5-6 ppb and PAC
LV at 1.5-2 ppb will be used to control the HPHT Fluid Loss below 5 ml/30min and keep the filter
cake as thin as possible on bore hole. 1-2 ppb Xanthan Gum provides both suspension capacity for
adding CaCO3-F as weight agent to reach desired MW and required cutting carrying capacity to clean
the hole. Use of Barite should be avoided as it can damage Ilam and Sarvak reservoirs. Although the
intervals of these two formations are going to be cased with 9⅝" casing, they are subject to be
perforated and their productivities are subject to be evaluated as secondary targets after Fahliyan
reservoir tested.
Based on well bore condition and stability and Glycol, as shale inhibitor is going to be mixed
equivalent of 2-3% by volume 100 m before we reach the top of Pabdeh formation. It should be a
Medium-Cloud Point Glycol with the primary function of shale inhibition for water-based muds. It
can be used while drilling Pabdeh and Laffan shales without further maintaining to let it be depleted
from the system gradually.
Centrifuges and hydrocyclones should be kept running to keep Low Gravity Solids content below 7%
in order to minimize reactive solids and improve ROP.
At section TD, minimum 1.2 times of annular volume circulation should be done prior to make a
wiper trip to surface. Monitoring the shakers for being clear of cutting helps in deciding when to stop
circulation.

Solids Control Management

    Shakers to be dressed initially with proper mesh screens (175/200 mesh size) to minimize
         the increment of fine solids in mud system.
    There may be a requirement to dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of
         circulations in order to minimize over flow of mud at the beginning of this section and to
        allow full dispersion of hydratable polymers.
    Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All
          efforts should be made to maintain the LGS content below 7%.

Interval Key Issues

   Drill the cement inside the casing to one or two meters before 13⅜” casing shoe, then pump
       Hi-Vis pill as a sweep.
   Maintain the Yield Point in the range 15-25 lb/100ft² to ensure adequate hole cleaning.
        Cuttings should be circulated up far above the BHA prior to connections. It should also be
        considered to ream at each connection. This will minimize the potential of cuttings settling
        during connections, causing packing off and stuck pipe. Prior any trips hole should be
        circulated to be cleaned and at least 1.2 times of bottoms-up. This will prevent tight hole on
        the way out and bridges, fill etc. on the way back in.

Mixing Procedure

   1. Fill tanks with calculated amount of Seawater 0.881 bbl/bbl

   2. Treat Drill water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash

   3. Mix 5-6 ppb Starch NF and 1.5-2 ppb PAC LV at rate of 1 sack per 7 min

   4. Mix NaCl at 77 ppb

   5. Xanthan Gum at range of 1-2 ppb at rate of 1 sack per 15 min

   6. Adjust mud weight as per hole condition by adding CaCO3-Fine

Note: As it was mentioned above, KCl, Glycol and Sulfonated Asphalt are not planned to be mixed
in initial preparation of mud. They are supposed to be added in case of hole dictation in the system as
per below plan:

    KCl
    To be added 100 m prior to reach Pabdeh formation due to probable losses of Asmari. It
      will be mixed at initial concentration of 15 ppb, but is supposed to be maintained in range
     10-15 ppb to section TD, unless hole condition dictates otherwise.
    Glycol
     Based on hole condition can be added while drilling through Pabdeh formation and Laffan
     formation (Optional). In each of these formations, it will be mixed at initial concentration
      of 2-3% by volume without further maintaining to let it be depleted gradually, unless hole
      condition dictates otherwise.

Properties Discussion

Mud Weight
Mud weigh has been planned for this section to be at range of 75-85 pcf. Controlling of MW could
be done by running hydrodyclones and centrifuges and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens
and dumping mud from sand trap and dilution instead.

Plastic Viscosity
Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment,
coupled with whole new mud dilution.( Predicted Optimum range is 6-22Cp but definite range shall
be obtained by Pilot test) .

Fluid Loss

                                                                             Page 104 of 240

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 105 of 240 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

It is recommended that API Fluid Loss be maintained below 7 ml/30min during the section. This is
be achieved by the addition of a combination of Starch NF at 5 ppb and PAC LV at 2 ppb.

Rheology
Maintain the Yield Point in the range of 15 to 25 lb/100ft² to ensure having adequate hole cleaning,
making adjustment with fresh mud or water as required. Thixotropic characteristic of the fluid is
supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized rheological profile with elevated low-
shear-rate-viscosity and high shear-thinning characteristics which result in fluid with yield point
greater than plastic viscosity.

Total Hardness
Total hardness should be maintained below 600 mg/lit for optimum polymer performance with the
addition of Soda Ash and Caustic Soda.

pH and Alkalinity
pH should be maintained in the range of 9 to 10 using Caustic Soda. This will maximize chemicals
performance and minimize corrosion problems.

MBT
Measuring of the MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT of range of below 7 is
acceptable. Using fine screens and high speed centrifuges will help in maintaining lower values of
MBT by discarding the fine solids and consequently minimizes the dilution rate.

Shale and Clay Inhibition
Shale and Clay inhibition will be achieved by utilizing KCl at range of 15-25 lb/bbl and Glycol at
range of 2-3% by volume.

Drilling Issues

Stuck Pipe
Evidences of tight hole and stuck pipe occurred in some wells while drilling this Section. Mud must
be inhibited to avoid the reaction with the shale and proper mud weight must be controlled. The main
actions to take in order to avoid differential sticking are tight fluid loss control, and continuous
movement of pipe and controlling mud weight. In the event of stuck pipe, environment-friendly pipe-
freeing pill can be spotted around the stuck area. The other candidate in this case can be using HCl
10-15%. Because of undesired side effect damage to metallic parts and hole wash out, using acid is
only considered for highly dramatic situations.

Hole Cleaning
Xanthan Gum is the base for Rheology in the KCl Polymer system. If additional Rheology is required,
increase Xanthan Gum concentration to enhance hole cleaning. Xanthan Gum will be used to provide
an optimized rheological profile with elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and high shear-thinning
characteristics which result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

Carbon Dioxide
Although it is unlikely to detect Carbon Dioxide in this section, based on an established protocol, the
mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically CO2. In case of Carbon
Dioxide contamination, Lime should be added at 0.5-2 ppb in order to remove CO2 in the form of
precipitating Calcium Carbonate.

Hydrogen Sulphide
Regardless that the interval has or has not the potential of emitting any gas, this is an established
protocol that the mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically H2S. If
any trace of H2S is detected, treat the mud with 1-2 ppb Zinc Carbonate and increase pH by Caustic
Soda to maintain it around 10. Corrosion Inhibitor should be used in this case at range of minimum
1% by volume.

Lubricity
In case of high torque and drag, Lubricant can be used at range of 1-2% by volume. This lubricant
should be of the type of Water-Dispersible Readily Biodegradable which provides the characteristics
string wet-ability by reduction of surface tension. This results in less chance of bit and BHA balling
and enhances ROP.

Downhole Losses
Losses/Differential sticking will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized
bridging/weight material (and Polymer) in conjunction with appropriate drilling practices. If seepage
losses are noted on the well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate is to
be made. For moderate loss rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150 micron is recommended to
ensure that there is adequate correctly sized material to act as bridging agents.
CaCO3 will minimize filtrate/whole mud invasion of the reservoir and reduce potential problems of
losses and differential sticking. The fluid loss and cake quality are two of the most important mud
properties to prevent or alleviate potential stuck pipe. Note that, the maintenance of the correct amount
and size of bridging material cannot be over-stressed.

    Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl/hr.
No specific action will be taken, but close monitoring of the probable loss rate is made.

    Losses 10-30 bbl/hr:

    Load CaCO3-M in active system up to 5-7 ppb
    Load CaCO3-C in active system up to 5-7 ppb

If no success, then:
    Pump 50 bbl LCM pill containing:
  7 ppb CaCO3-M
  7 ppb CaCO3-C
  5 ppb Mica Medium
  5 ppb Walnut Shells Fine
  5 ppb Kwik-Seal Fine
  5 ppb CaCO3-M
Note: System is loaded gradually from low concentration to maximum mentioned ranges.

    Losses 30-100 bbl/hr:

    Load CaCO3-M in active system up to 7 ppb
    Load CaCO3-C in active system up to 7 ppb
    Load Kwik-Seal F in system up to 5 ppb

    Shaker-man should be ready for managing a part of the return flow toward the pit-
       room by-pass shakers to avoid screens get blinded and LCM get wasted.

If no success, then:

    Stop Drilling
    Pull out string above the loss zone
    Spot 60-90 bbl pill containing:
   Pre-Hydrated Bentonite 5-10 ppb
  30 lb/bbl CaCO3-F,M
  10 lb/bbl Kwik-Seal F
  10 lb/bbl Kwik-Seal M
  10 lb/bbl Walnut-Shells F

  10 lb/bbl Mica M
   Repeat the pill twice
    If LCM pill at above concentration cannot pass through the string (bit nuzzles, etc.), we need
         to pump the pill through a Mule-Shoe while following the procedure of the next state.

    Losses more than 100 bbl/hr to Total Losses:

In the event of severe losses, Squeeze Pills, Barite or CaCO3 or Cement Plugs, Silicate Pill or Cross-
Linking Pills should be pumped to minimize losses.

    LCM Pill Application Procedure

   1. After spotting LCM pill over thief zone, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30
     minutes and monitor the annulus. After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full.
   2. If the hole can be filled, close the BOP and squeeze 10 bbl of LCM pill into the formation without
     exceeding 200 psi.
   3. If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.
   4. If the LCM pill failed to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and spot another
     50 bbl of LCM pill.
   5. Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbl of LCM pill into the
     formation without exceeding 200 psi.
   6. If a squeeze pressure develops, hold pressure for 1 hour before running the string back to bottom.

Notes:
    All LCM pills must be thoroughly mixed and homogenized and enough viscous
           before pumping.
    Remove filter screens from the drill pipe and if necessary, remove the strainers
         from the mud pumps suction lines.

Interval Threats / Barriers

     Threat            Barriers

     Personnel Safety   Ensure that all PPE as specified in MSDS is worn when mixing/ handling
      using Chemicals   Mud Chemicals.

     Downhole Loss     Losses can be experienced in whole section; Close monitoring shall be

     Gas Influx         Maintain proper mud weight.

          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 116 of 240 053-073-9125

This section will be drilled at mud weight 100 to 106 pcf and Salt Saturated/ KCl/ Glycol/ Polymer/
CaCO3/ Mud system will be used. The possible risks of this section are downhole losses, flow of gas
and/or oil and tight hole which may lead to stuck pipe. Severe losses were experienced in porous
layers, especially in Fahlian formation.
Starch HT at 5-6 ppb will be used to control the API Fluid Loss below 5-3 ml/30min and keep the
filter cake as thin as possible. Differential Stuck pipes can be encountered in this section therefore it
is vital to keep thin filter cake.
Xanthan Gum is used as the base of a thixotropic Rheology to provide adequate YP and high LSRV
(Low Shear Rate Viscosity) and high-shear-thinning-viscosity which are the key factors to ensure
adequate hole cleaning.

Mud Weight
   1. Mud Density vs. Reservoir Consideration

   Density of base water will be increased by combination of Salt (65 ppb) and KCl (9.5 ppb) to get
   brine at density of 75.5 pcf, then for increasing the density up to 82 pcf, CaCO3-F will be utilized.

Rheology
   Thixotropic characteristic of the fluid is supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized
   rheological profile with elevated low-shear rate-viscosity and high-shear-thinning characteristics
  which result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity. Plastic viscosity should be
   maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with new mud
   dilution.

Water-Dispersible Lubricant
    It should be an environmentally friendly, biodegradable and non-damaging lubricant which
   increases the lubricity of the system and reduces the torque and drag, compatible with most water-
   based muds. It is formulated at range of 1-2% by volume in this interval.

Clay-based Lithology Inhibition; a matter of caring reservoir as well
  Potassium Chloride is used as a Clay/Shale Inhibitor where clay can be existing in limestone
   layered. The concentration required will be based on the extent of the clay but will generally vary
  from 3-5% by weight in the system. Use of KCl in reservoir mud has also the good effect of
  minimizing the hydration and consequently swelling of the clay-based lithology of the pore’s walls.
   This helps in less damage to the reservoir caused by inevitable mud invasion.

Bio-Cide
   Starch HT, PAC LV and Xanthan Gum are subject to bacterial degradation even in saturated brines,
   therefore, a biocide should be used in the system to retard this happening and extend lift-time of
   the said products.

Solids Control Management

   Shakers to be dressed initially with proper mesh screens (200/230 mesh size). There may be
        a requirement to dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order
         to minimize surface loss of mud.
   Combination of  linear motion shale shakers with centrifuges proved best  results.  If
         centrifuges are planned to run it should be noted that there is the risk discarding CaCO3.
       Running retort test on samples of centrifuged fluids gives ideas on how justifiable the plan
            is.
   Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All
          efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 7%.

Interval Key Issues

   Mud weight in this interval is critical for wellbore stability and successful drilling and hole
        condition will dictate the mud density.
   Cuttings should be circulated up above the BHA prior to connections. It should also be
        considered to ream at each connection. This will minimize the potential of cuttings settling
        during connections, causing packing off and stuck pipe. Prior to trips the hole should be
         circulated for at least 1.5 times of annular volume circulation should be done prior to make
        a wiper trip to surface. Monitoring the shakers for being clear of cutting helps in deciding
       when to stop circulation. This will prevent tight hole on the way out and bridges, fill etc. on
         the way back in.
   Maintain a contingency stock of Caustic Soda, Zinc Carbonate, Lime, Citric Acid, Barite,
        Hematite and fine and medium size of acid-soluble LCM on board.
   Total Hardness content in the filtrate should be controlled less than 600 mg/lit by using Soda
       Ash and Caustic Soda for better performance of polymers.
   Use pre-mixes to maintain system volumes and to make necessary dilutions. The pre-mixes
         will contain sufficient polymers to replace polymers lost by either degradation or adsorption
         to drilled cuttings.

Mixing Procedure

   1. Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.722 bbl/bbl

   2. Treat Drill Water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash

   3. Mix 5-6 ppb Starch HT, at rate of 1 sack per 7 min

   4. Mix KCl at 9.5 ppb and NaCl at 65 ppb

   5. In case of what hole dictates, Addition of pH-Buffer, Oxygen Scavenger S, Corrosion Inhibitor,
     ZnCO3, Bio-Cide is while drilling as required.

   6. Add CaCO3-F (256ppb) to reach MW of ±100 pcf

    In case of foaming use Alcohol-Based Defoamer.

    In case of excessive torque use Lubricant at range of 1-2% by volume.

Properties Discussion

Rheology
   Thixotropic characteristic of the fluid is supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized
   rheological profile with elevated low-shear rate-viscosity and high-shear-thinning characteristics
  which result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity. Plastic viscosity should be
   maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with new mud
   dilution.

Fluid Loss
   It is recommended that the API Fluid Loss be maintained at <5-3 ml/30min. This may best be
  achieved by the addition of 6 ppb Starch HT. Offering other High-Temp Drill-In Fluid Loss
   controllers is welcome and usage is subject to be investigated.

Total Hardness
  Total hardness should be maintained below 600 mg/lit for optimum polymer performance with the
  addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda.

pH and Alkalinity

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 120 of 240 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

  PH should be maintained in the range of 9 to 10.5 using Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda. This will
  maximize chemicals performance and minimize corrosion problems.

Drilling Issues

Stuck Pipe

  The main actions to take in order to avoid differential sticking are tight fluid loss control, and
  continuous movement of pipe and controlling mud weight. In the event of stuck pipe, environment-
   friendly pipe-freeing pill can be spotted around the stuck area. The other candidate in this case can
  be using HCl 10-15%. Because of undesired side effect damage to metallic parts and hole wash
   out, using acid is only considered for highly dramatic situations.

Hole Cleaning

  The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning, are VG-meter 6 and 3 dial readings. Prior to
  connections, the cuttings should be circulated well above the bottom hole assembly to avoid
  packing off after connections. Hole should be circulated clean before starting to POOH or back
  reaming.

    Parameters affecting Hole Cleaning:

   1. Monitoring shakers to become clear of cutting is a key factor to judge if the hole is clean.

   2. Pump as fast as possible.

   3. Control ROP's must be considered to avoid heavy load of cuttings in annulus.

   4. In laminar flow the hole cleaning capacity, especially at low shear rates in large diameter
      sections, can be improved by raising the low shear-rate viscosity & gels. The best indicators
      will be the 6 & 3 rpm and initial gel.

Lubricity

   In case of high torque and drag, Lubricant can be used at range of 1-2% by volume. This lubricant
   should be of the type of environment-friendly water-dispersible readily biodegradable which
   provides the characteristics of string wet-ability by reduction of surface tension. This results in less
  chance of bit and BHA balling and enhances ROP.

Hydrogen Sulphide

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 121 of 240 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

   Regardless that the interval has or has not the potential of emitting any gas, this is an established
   protocol that the mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically H2S.
   If any trace of H2S is detected, treat the mud with 1-2 ppb Zinc Carbonate and increase pH by
   Caustic Soda or Lime to maintain it around 10. Corrosion Inhibitor should be used in this case at
   range of minimum 1% by volume.

Carbon Dioxide

  Although it is unlikely to detect Carbon Dioxide in this section, based on an established protocol,
   the mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically CO2. In case of
  Carbon Dioxide contamination, Lime should be added at 0.5-2 ppb in order to remove CO2 in the
  form of precipitating Calcium Carbonate.

Downhole Losses

   Losses/Differential sticking will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized
  bridging/weight material (and Polymer) in conjunction with appropriate drilling practices.  If
  seepage losses are noted on the well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the
   loss rate is to be made. For moderate loss rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150 micron is
  recommended to ensure that there is adequate correctly sized material to act as bridging agents.
  CaCO3 will minimize filtrate/whole mud invasion of the reservoir and reduce potential problems
  of losses and differential sticking. The fluid loss and cake quality are two of the most important mud
   properties to prevent or alleviate potential stuck pipe. Note that, the maintenance of the correct
  amount and size of bridging material cannot be over-stressed.

 Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl/hr

  No specific action will be taken, but close monitoring of the probable loss rate is made.

 Losses from 10-30 bbl/hr

   Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb
   Since some of the CaCO3-M will be discarded over the shakers, add 100 kg per 10 meter drilled
       to compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

    If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:
    Pump 40-60 bbl of pill made by 7-10 ppb CaCO3 150-300μ & 7-10 ppb CaCO3 600μ

────────────────────────────────────────────

 Losses from 30-50 bbl/hr

   Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb
   Since some of the CaCO3-M will be discarded over the shakers, add 100 kg per 10 meter drilled
       to compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

       If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:
    Pump 40-60 bbl of pill made by
     10-20 ppb CaCO3 200-300μ
     10-20 ppb CaCO3 600 μ
     10pbb Oyster Shell-F
     10pbb Oyster Shell-M

 Losses from 50-100 bbl/hr

     Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb
     Load CaCO3-C (600-100 micron) in system up to 5 ppb
      Since some of the CaCO3-M&C will be discarded over the shakers, add 100 kg per 10
          meter drilled to compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

        If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:
     Pump 40-60 bbl of the following pill:
            10-20 ppb CaCO3 200-300 micron
            10-20 ppb CaCO3 600 micron
            7-10 ppb of each CaCO3 1000 micron & CaCO3 2000 micron
            5-10 pbb Oyster Shell -F
            5-10 pbb Oyster Shell -M

 Losses more than 100 bbl/hr

      High concentrated LCM pill of various sizes of Calcium Carbonate and Oyster Shell-
    F&M&C should be pumped and spotted and gently squeezed over the loss zone.

     Spotting Procedure

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 123 of 240 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

    1.  After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30 minutes
      and monitor the annulus.
    2.  After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full. If the hole can be filled,
       close BOP and squeeze 10 bbl LCM pill into formation without exceeding 200 psi.
    3.  If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.
    4.  Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and
       spot another 50 bbl of LCM pill.
    5.  Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbl of LCM pill
        into the formation without exceeding 200 psi.
    6.  If a squeeze pressure develops, hold the pressure for 1 hour before running the drill string
      back to bottom.

Notes:
   LCM pills must be thoroughly homogenised and viscous enough before being pumped.
   Pumping high-concentrated LCM pill is subject to use of open-end DP or Mule-Shoe.
      Use of PBL Sub is a good practice too.
   Remove filter screens from the drill pipe (if there is any) and if necessary, remove
        strainers from the mud pump suction lines.

Logging, Casing Running & Cementing

It is most importance that the hole is clean prior to logging and running liner. Any adjustments to mud
properties, such as reduction of gel strength, before logging and before running liner will be discussed.
Make pit management plan for dealing with returns from running and cementing casing, with
contingencies or lost circulation and dealing with spacer returns and contaminated mud. Reduce yield
point to minimum level (if practical) prior to cement job.

    Completion Phase

Note: Completion fluid specification will be prepared by Mahan Sanat Arya in completion
program and after client approval will be implemented.

Fluid#1: Completion Fluid
Clear, solids-free brines are the most commonly used fluids in completion and work over operations
to minimize formation damage whilst perforation job and completion phase to improve production
rate. Completion and work over fluids are specialized fluids used during well completion operations
and remedial workover procedures. These fluids must control not only subsurface pressure with
density, but also must minimize formation damage during completion and workover operations. The
use of fluids that cause minimal formation damage can result in improved production. Most reservoirs
are sensitive to any fluids other than those contained in them naturally.

At the beginning, all surface pits and all involved lines need to be cleaned and flushed thoroughly,
then hole is supposed to be displaced with inhibited CaBr2 Brine at density of 105 pcf (last mud weight
applied in drilling 8 ½” section), to be ready for completing the well.

Density:
   Density of this completion fluid is to be provided by readily commercial liquid Calcium Bromide
   with initial density of 14.2 ppg (= 106 pcf = 1702 kg/m3). It is used for blending clear brine,
  workover brine and completion fluids. It is supplied in 55 gal drums. Note that, when consulting
   salt tables for formulating the fluid, the inevitable drop of density due to addition of corrosion
   inhibitor should be considered.

   Quality and specifications of CaBr2 shall meet the criteria of a standard regulation to be announced
  and conformity of the product to be supplied with the regulation is subject to be confirmed through
  an approved third-party quality testing evidence. Some very common and must-meet specs of an
  approved sample of commercial Calcium Bromide are as below:

                Identity:                     Calcium Bromide Liquid, 14.2 SG
                Structural Formula:                 Br-Ca-Br;HOH
               Molecular Formula:                 CaBr2;H20
               Molecular Weight:                    199.9
               CaBr2 %:                52% by weight
               Boiling Point:               129°C (265°F)
               Bulk Density:                 ~14.2 lb/gal (1.70 - 1.73 SG) at 25°F
                Solubility in Water:                    Miscible

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 128 of 240 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

               Appearance and Odor:          Clear fluid, Colorless liquid with no odor
                Turbidity:                   6 NTU maximum
               pH Value:                   7 ±1
                Crystallization Temperature:    -12.2°C (10°F) Approx.
               Corrosion Rate:             < 5 MPY maximum

Corrosion:
   Salt solutions are often highly corrosive. Dissolved oxygen and massive concentration of ions are
   the primary corrosive agents in sodium-, potassium-, calcium-chloride- or bromide-brine base
   completion fluids. The solubility of oxygen in these brines decreases as saturation with the salt is
   approached. Anyhow corrosion inhibitor at concentration of 1% by volume and oxygen scavenger
   (special type compatible with Calcium brines) at concentration of 0.5 ppb should be added in
   completion fluid to minimize the risk of corrosion.

  Appearance of some corrosion inhibitors available in market is amber in color and slightly dark
   (not 100% clear). Using these types of product may cause reading the turbidity somehow more
   than what recorded before adding it. Selecting a type of corrosion inhibitor that besides providing
   the expected metal protection characteristics causes excess value of NTU as less as possible is a
   point which needs to be considered.

Dissolved Oxygen:
   In order to eliminate the threat of dissolved oxygen as a possible source of corrosion, use of Oxygen
  Scavenger CA is formulated in completion fluid at concentration of 0.5 ppb. Oxygen Scavenger
  CA is a catalyzed Sodium-based chemical used to scavenge oxygen dissolved in Calcium Brines
  and also drilling fluids having more than 300 ppm filtrate Calcium. It lowers the risk of corrosion
  and extends the life of metallic parts including production tubing. It is a stable solid and does not
   deteriorate when exposed to the atmosphere for extended periods of time.

  Oxygen Scavengers must be added directly through the hatch from the top of suction pit, not
   using/running mixing pump and just prior to pump the fluid into the well. Although, the
   concentration is very little, since this stage is after filtering the brine, it is recommended to do a
   pilot test in lab to ensure turbidity remains in acceptable range after adding this material.

H2S Scavenger:
  Use of liquid H2S scavenger, as a preventive safety factor, is recommended to be added at
   concentration of 0.5%by volume completion fluid. It should be of the type designed specifically
   for brine-base fluid systems to remove H2S.

       Mixing Procedure; Completion Fluid (based on 105 pcf using only CaBr2)

    1. Make sure that all pits and lines involved with completion fluid are thoroughly cleaned,
       flushed and free of any fluid and solid.
    Make sure that at least one large pit is kept empty for transferring ready brine
            into after given time for settling. After transferring one pit to empty pit, the first
         one is to be flushed and cleaned for accommodating the brine of next ready pit,
         and so on to the last pit.
    Depends on the rig facilities and structure, mud engineer on board may find it
            better to prepare the fluids pit-by-pit.
    2.  Transfer the content of CaBr2 drums into designated pits.
    Record the number of drums poured in each tank for accurate volume in it as
           the base of calculation for adding other additives into; do not rely on pit gauge,
          sounding or mud logging sensor, but have a look on them for comparison and/or
           correlation if found useful.
    3. Mix Corrosion Inhibitor into pits at concentration of 3.5pbb (1% by volume).
    4. Mix H2S Scavenger Liquid into pits at concentration of 0.5% by Volume.
    5. Do not add Oxygen Scavenger CA at this stage as it should be added directly from the
       top of the pit, just prior to pump the fluid into the well.
    6.  Shut down all agitators and mixing pumps, and leave the mixed fluid in the pits for at
        least 12 hours to let any solid particle inside settles down.
    7.  Start transferring the clear fluid of the first pit to the empty pit by means of an air-
      powered Wilden pump.
    Make sure that the suction hose of the Wilden pump is not put deep close to the
          bottom of the pit, otherwise, settled solids are sucked in.
    8.  After finishing the first pit, stop Wilden pump, wash, flush and clean the pit, use it as
       the empty pit for accommodating the fluid of second pit using the and same above
      method.
TSS (Total Suspended Solids) and Turbidity (NTU: Nephelomertric Turbidity Units) of a fluid are
the parameters that are used to express the extent to which the fluid is free of solids. These factors are
measured on wellsite using a HACH® Test Kit. Most of the operations, require TSS and NTU ranging

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 130 of 240 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

up to 40. Here, we need TSS<30 and NTU<40 for the fluid pumping in the well and both TSS and
NTU less than 100 for the returned fluid.
For the fluids we are going to work with, i.e. packer fluid and CaBr2 completion fluid, typically, there
is a high chance of getting desired low value of TSS and NTU easily, because they are made with
clear liquid CaBr2, not powder, therefore, there is no impurity in the form of solid
Fluid#2: Packer Fluid
Packer Fluid, here, is suggested to be basically CaBr2 brine same as completion fluid introduced
earlier.

Fluid#3: Non-Solid Hi-Vis Pill

Generally, we prepare and use different types of Hi-Viscous pills based on the specifications of the
two fluids behind and ahead of the pills and the probable limitations applicable, e.g. the concern of
di-valent/mono-valent salts, or remarkably different densities.
If one of the two fluids is CaBr2 brine, the suggestion for the Hi-Vis pill is to make it using a batch of
saturated CaCl2 brine (86 pcf = 11.5 ppg) in which Hydroxy Ethyl Cellulose (HEC) is mixed as the
viscosifier.
HEC is a modified high-molecular-weight. Non-ionic natural polymer especially suited for the
viscosity of brine. This non-fermenting polymer increases viscosity and carrying capacity of
workover and completion fluids and heavy brines.
HEC is used to viscosify single salt CaCl2 brines and all mono-valent-salt brines such as NaCl, NaBr,
KCl, etc. While mixing, it shows no tendency to form fisheyes and rapidly and smoothly get viscous
without the need for high shear mixing. The H-Vis pill made by HEC has a short lifetime and overtime
the polymer may become separated from the carrier fluid, therefore, it should be only prepared upon
requirement and for the needed volume. Routine usage of HEC is at concentration of ±2 ppb, at pH
range of 7 to 9.

Fluid#4: Non-Solid Spacer

Due to having a sensitive completion fluid, in terms of cost, density and being non-solid, use of spacer
between every two batches of different fluids to be pumped is a must. Here, the spacer is designed to
be again saturated CaCl2 brine (86 pcf = 11.5 ppg). This is heaviest cost-effective non-solid fluid
which can be prepared to play the role of a spacer on one end exposed to CaBr2 completion fluid. In
the other side, since both CaBr2 and CaCl2 are di-valent salts of the same cation (Calcium) there is no
risk of forming precipitation as a result of touching two brines of di-valent and mono-valent salts.
This CaCl2 Brine spacer is simply made of 0.823 bbl/bbl fresh water in which 193 ppb of CaCl2 95%
purity is solved. No any other additive needs to be used.
