    9.  Casing Program

         Material Selection

     Casing, Liner and Tubing Material selection for South Azadegan oilfield will be
      describe in the following.
    Corrosive Environment Analysis and Strength Check

     Based on the data of offset wells in  this  oilfield, there  is a certain degree
      of  corrosive problems  in  the 4  layers  to be produced.  Corrosive medium
       is  principally composed  of 2  parts: one  is  the  corrosive  gases  like H2S
     and CO2 existing in the produced  fluid; and the other  is the high  salinity
     formation water. The contents of main  corrosive  fluids  in  offset wells  are
     shown in below Table:

         1)  Corrosion in this oilfield is a result of combined action of H2S, CO2 and
            high salinity formation water. The corrosive mechanism is complicated, and
             the corrosive rate on the casing is difficult to determine. Based on the NACE
             standard and the data from the Table, the producers result in severe corrosive
            environment. However, by the research on development conditions and
             technical indices, it can be found that although the corrosive fluid contents
             are high in the oilfield, the corrosive environment is not extremely serious
             as the following reasons:

                                                                                   Page 147 of 240

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 148 of 240053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

         2)  In general, the temperature that cause the SSC/SCC is concentrated in the
            range from 20℃ to 30℃. The average depth of the horizontal section is
           2,730m with the reservoir temperature of 96℃, and tensional stress on the
             casing does not exist in the horizontal section. Therefore, the influence of
         SSC/SCC may not be considered for the casing/liner.

         3) Based on the RMDP, the production GOR in the first development phase
            should not be higher than the initial GOR, therefore, the flowing pressure is
             higher than the bubble point pressure all the time, that is, degassing problems
           do not exist in the horizontal section and some vertical section, the H2S and
         CO2 have no chance of separation out of oil phase, and  it is lack of
              prerequisite for casing corrosion.

         4) Based on above all, the corrosive environment of the casing string is not
             severe. The optimal selection for the casing string can be stated briefly as
             follows.

     Material Selection of Casing String

            In  this  oilfield,  the  corrosion  of  production  string  obviously  occurs
            in  2  regions. One  is  the  region  where  the  pressure  is  above  the
          bubble  point;  in  which  degassing  problems  do  not  exist,  and  the
           corrosion environment  is  relatively weak. Another one  is  the  region
          where the pressure  is below the bubble point; because of the decline
           of  pressure,  the  concentration  of  corrosive gas  will  increase and  the
           corrosion     is    relatively    serious.    Considering    the    corrosive
          environment  is not serious in the low water cut production stage and
            the production practice in this oilfield has proved the L80  is  fit for  it,
           So, the L80 should be taken as the material of 9-5/8″  casing,  7″, 5
           1/2″ and 4-1/2″  liner.  In order  to prevent  the hazard of gas leakage
             after production degassing  occurs,  9-5/8″  casing, 7″ and  4-1/2″  liner
           should be Gas tight thread. 2) The 110S  is selected as the material of
            9-5/8″, 7″ and4-1/2″ casing rather than L-80 due to the high strength

           requirement  in Fahliyan  wells, what’s more  the 110S  is  fit  for sour
           gas environment

                                   Table 10-2: H2S & CO2 Content in AZNS Offset Wells

                      formation               (mol%)

   AZN4            Kuzhdumi                    0                             2.62
                     Gadvan                                                      2.64
   AZN6             Gadvan                                                      2.47

   Considering the information above, API 6A 19th & NACE MR-0175 (2003) /ISO 1516, and Cl-
    content which is being most concerned, the South AZADEGA X-mas tree material and the tubing
   hanger should be FF0.5 class. As to the casing head, it’s barely exposed to resident fluid, or only
    for quite a short time, when it comes to desert working condition, according to API 6A19th &
   NACE-MR-0175 (2003) /ISO 1516, the tubing spool should be EE0.5, the casing head material
    class should be DD0.5 (ANSI 4130) , stainless steel cladding in ring groove

C.  Selection of PR (Performance Requirement)

According to API Specification 6A 19th edition, performance requirements are specific and unique
to the product in the as-shipped condition. All products shall be designed to perform according to
the requirements of API 6A clauses 4 and clauses 10 while in the pressure and temperature ranges
and corrosion environment. Other requirements include load capability, cycles, and operating force
or torque. There are two performance requirement levels: PR1 and PR2. Valves operating as safety
valves shall be of the PR2 performance level and meet the requirements of Annex I in API 6A For
SA wells, the guideline for PR selection is that all parts not contacting well fluids in normal
production period are PR1, all parts contacting well fluids are PR2 as follow, Casing head housing
and casing head spool assembly - PR1. Tubing head spool, tubing hanger and X-mas tree - PR2.

D. Temperature Class

Environment temp:
Well temp: 0.0244×4100+27.384=127℃
According to API 6A 19th, temp should be U (-18℃-121℃)

11. Waste Management Program

NOTE: The provision of Waste Management Engineering and Operational Services to drill Fahliyan
vertical oil producer well in South Azadegan oilfield and detailed WM program will be issued in due time.
As per SOW, waste management in this location is Zero discharge system and general waste management
plan will be described in advance.

    Introduction

The recommended waste management method for this proposal is dewatering process for fluids, and fixation
process for the generated cuttings and solids. Bulk dewatering system comprises of Mixing Hopper, waste
water conditioning tank, pumps, hoses, jet nozzles, chemicals etc. Purpose the bulk dewatering system is to
recycle all the waste fluids and dumped WBM which are generated as a result of drilling activity at top holes
in minimum time. Dewatering is the process of removing the majority of colloidal size of solids phase in
excess of used water base drilling fluid by the addition of chemicals to coagulate and flocculate the solids
in the mud thus blended chemically enhanced fluid is pumped to centrifuge. Processed solids will be
removed from the fluid and we would be received cleaned water at the end. The separated cuttings will be
disposed into the corral and cleaned water goes to storage tank for future utilization, or dumping out of the
rig site.
Without chemical enhancement or the dewatering process, the mechanical liquid solids separation capability
of a centrifuge is limited to 2-3 micron. Thus, dewatering overcomes this limitation by flocculation of the
feed mud by pre-treating chemically to increase the effective particle size of suspended solids. It is important
to consider that dewatering method focuses on separating liquid phase from solid phase, in the other words
we surely need to test the final water to make sure that it's not harmful for the environment or if it uses for
new drilling fluid mixing, the necessary parameters are suitable for this purpose.
Chemically Enhanced Centrifugation (CEC) system  is used to remove colloidal particles from non-
emulsified fluids such as water based drilling fluids that are too small to be removed by a decanting
centrifuge. By employing chemical techniques, the colloidal particles assume the size and mass that
facilitates separation by a decanting centrifuge.
The overall objective of a dewatering system is to process the drilling waste for:
1) Reduction of the liquid waste volume in drilling operation.
2) Recycling of the fluid to build new drilling fluid.
3) Dispose the processed waste to quarantine it from the environment.
4) Release in an environmentally safe and cost-effective manner.

Waste Fluid Management

        Fluid handling

All hazardous and non-hazardous fluids will have to be chemically treated prior to recycling/disposal. For

treating such fluids, stabilization or chemical flocculation is carried out.

In order to reduce the impact of the cuttings and mud to environment, the following procedure is proposed.

1) Reduce the extent of dilution. For achieving this goal, first-rate solids control equipment should be used

on the rig.

2) Salt-contaminated cuttings should be kept separate from the top-hole (non-hazardous) cuttings.

3) Similarly salt contaminated and water based fluids should be kept separate from the fluid discharged from

the top-hole sections.

4) Excess and end-of-well salt contaminated fluid should be processed through the DEWATERING

SYSTEM.

5) Stabilization and burial of the salt contaminated solids

Chemically Enhanced Centrifugation (CEC) System

Traditional methods of removing ultrafine solids from drilling fluids utilizing chemical techniques either
rely upon a batch approach or by using separate pieces of equipment to dose dilute and treat. The batch
approach is inefficient, as overdosing with expensive chemicals is possible. Also, controlling the feed
conditions for centrifuge processing is difficult. Using separate pieces of equipment to dilute, dose and treat
is an improved method but has the disadvantages of increased installation time and cost. The Chemically
Enhanced Centrifugation (CEC) System eliminates both of these problems by offering real-time fluid
treatment as an integrated package. The CEC System allows the operator to use dry-form Coagulant and
Flocculants; this significantly reduces the purchase and transportation costs when compared to liquid form
chemicals. The CEC System is the culmination of over two decades experience and offers an efficient
method of colloidal particle treatment
If the dewatering system runs properly and we have an effective utilization, it can reduce disposal cost by
more than 40% which is remarkable amount. Dewatering process involves:
1) Coagulation
2) Flocculation

3) Settling
4) Mechanical solids removal
As it's mentioned, in dewatering process two types of chemicals will be used:
a) Coagulant agent, such as: Poly aluminum chloride / Liquid or Powder
b) Flocculent agent, such as: Polyelectrolyte (Polymer) / Powder

        Coagulation

     Coagulation is the addition of chemicals to water causing colloidal particles within the Water to stick
      or bond together when contact is made. Mixing is utilized during the coagulation to provide a rapid
     and uniform dispersion of the chemicals and also increase the opportunity for particle to particle
      contact. Normally, the entire process occurs in less than one second.

        Flocculation
Flocculation generally follows coagulation and can be described as a chemical and physical bridging or
agglomeration of the coagulation particles. The flocculation process involves gently mixing the particles
until distinct, suspended flocks are formed.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
           South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                             Document Title
    Contract No:
                            Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 177 of 240    053-073-9125
                  SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

Mixing polymer  is more important to consider, improper preparation of a polymer can affect the
performance and efficiency of the flocculation process, thereby drastically raising the cost of the polymer
usage for the project. With this in mind, the mixing system, although a simple process, must be designed
and engineered properly and professionally for successful operation. To reach this aim, the agitation must
have sufficient force to achieve these requirements, but have no centers of high shear which would damage
the flocculant molecules. It's important to consider that the polymers typically need about 30 minutes of
aging after being blended with water to allow for proper hydration and release of the free chains, due to this
point in some plant a batch mixing system is recommended which allows polymer aging before being
utilized in the process.
Delivering the polymer to targeted waste is another important factor, adding the polymer to the waste should
be without damage to polymer chain to have proper flocculation, in the other words we do need maximum
contact between polymer and particles in the fluid.
Another considerable issue is running pilot test before starting the operation, the objective of the pilot testing
is to determine the most effective and economic dosage of the chemical for the process for a given fluid
system. Efficiency simply means the best coagulant and flocculants that we are able to have, and economics
will be based on the number of chemicals and concentration of each required in order to obtain satisfactory
results.
The effectiveness of various chemicals is subjective, based on the size and stability of the flocs and clarity
of the resultant liquid. No doubt that we should run different numbers of tests to assure that there is no
impact against the environmental in the discharged fluid. The most important tests which have to be done

Recovered water
There are three final destinations available for the generated water from dewatering unit:
   1) Using 50% in the drilling fluid mixing.
   2) Discharged water after dewatering should meet below standards:
           pH = 7-9
          COD < 200 mg/lit, BOD < 300 mg/lit
           Ca2+ < 600 mg/lit
           Hardness < 800 mg/lit
           Turbidity < 50 ntu
           TSS < 85 mg/l
           Color (Color unit, chromaticity)
           IPS-E-SF-880 Standard
   2) Washing jobs around the rig.
   3) Disposing into a designated area (disposal area), for this purpose, a written confirmation will be
      required from environmental department of the region/state which states that there is no problem to
    dump the fluid into the disposal area at all.

Solids Control Equipment on the Rig

All the cutting which is generated from solids control equipment and dewatering centrifuge or any other

method for this purpose is named Fixation. Actually, Solidification and Stabilization are classified as
fixation process when the main purpose is to immobilize or isolate the contaminated solids. One of the most
important and vital purpose of fixation is avoid chloride contamination of environmental specifically

        Shale Shakers

The first and most important criterion in solids control system design is the removal of the maximum amount
of drilled solids at the first available opportunity with the minimum of mechanical handling. This can be
achieved by maximizing the screening area available at the flow-line. Failure to do so results in excessive
and unnecessary use of hydro-cyclones that create fines due to particle degradation in the centrifugal feed
pump and the cones having low work share efficiency with high fluid loss.

       Desander / Desilter

In Fluid Management Desander / Desilter should only be utilized for 2 to 3 circulations when there is more
than 1-2% sand or an excessively high level of L.G.S solids in the mud. Hydrocyclones were first introduced
to process 125% - 150% of the circulating volumes in un-weighted mud, but due to the particle degradation
in the centrifugal feed pump, many ultrafine and colloidal solids are created and returned to the mud system.
The cone underflow should then be screened over the shale shakers.

        Centrifuges

Most important criteria in the function of centrifuges are the ability to maximize the operational process.
Centrifuges are generally installed with the ability to only process drilling fluid. On the work over rig one
set of centrifuge will be needed to control fluid density and yield point. If we have low mud weight we don't
need barite recovery system on the rig, but in the case of heavy mud barite recovery will be run under proper
setting.

     Mud Cleaner

It’s a combination of one shale shaker with desander and desilter. It’ll be used for un-weighted fluids, its
important advantage is preventing of high loss which normally occurs in running desander and desilter.
Selecting proper mesh screen is a point, 325 mesh size or finer (up to 440) would be suitable for mud cleaner
in most of the drilling fields.
The mentioned equipment are the common on almost all drilling rigs, but if any special device or equipment
requires during the operation (for instance: gumbo chain, super-colon or etc.), it could be ordered to be ready
and installed.

              of its safety performance.

              Representative shall be given a copy of the minutes of the meetings.

        Environmental Management

       COMPANY shall comply with any and all laws, rules and regulations of
             governmental agencies having  jurisdiction, which now  exist or may be
             promulgated during the term of the CONTRACT, relating to the control and
              prevention of damage to the environment.
       Without prejudice to above, COMPANY shall ensure that all personnel use the
              highest prevailing standards of care and diligence to prevent unlawful disposal
              of all waste oil, water and other waste materials or fluids which may accumulate
              or be caused by COMPANY’s performance of the CONTRACT. COMPANY
                shall not dispose of any objects, scrap, waste, rubbish, equipment, fluids or fuel
               into the surrounding area or allow anything to be stored loose where it can be
              driven into surrounding areas by wind. COMPANY shall take all reasonable
              precautions to prevent pollution of any nature or kind from its performance of
               the WORK. COMPANY shall have contingency plans and procedures in place
               for such events.
       In the event of any disposal prohibited by Item 3.2 above, whether by dumping,
                spilling, emission or otherwise arising from COMPANY’s performance or non-
             performance of the CONTRACT, COMPANY shall be fully liable for and bear
               the costs of removal of any such item(s) dumped, spilled, emitted or otherwise
              disposed regardless of the sole, concurrent or contributory negligence or breach
              of duty (statutory or otherwise) of PPL/PEDEC. In the event of any such
               disposal, COMPANY shall immediately undertake all reasonable remedial and
               protective measures required in such circumstances.
       COMPANY  shall  notify PPL/PEDEC immediately with  respect  to any
               pollution, loss, damage, claim or demand (or occurrence which may give rise
               to the same) resulting from the CONTRACT. COMPANY shall report to
          PPL/PEDEC any incidents of non-compliance with legislative and regulatory
             environmental requirements that occur during the performance of the WORK.
             Without relieving COMPANY of any of its obligations under Item 3.2, if
        COMPANY does not promptly proceed to perform its obligations under this

       Prior to spud mud pit and sewage pit must comply with the standard. Install
              cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump and sewage
               circulating system for cleaning rig floor and equipment.
       Install BOP stack and pressure test shall be operated according to the drilling
              design to avoid blowout.
       Install oil supply lines and check whether there is any leakage.

    Management of environment protection on location:
       In drilling operation keep mud and sewage from overflowing. If it happens,
              clean up timely.
       Mud chemicals shall be stored according to the standard and shall not be
               scattered around well site. If mud chemicals scatter while loading or
              unloading, clean it up at once. The sack of mud chemicals shall be recovered.
          Do not dispose it on site.
       Enhance water management at well location and do not wash equipment with
               fresh water. Stop water flowing for long time. Overhead tanks shall be
                utilized.
       Oil management shall be carefully at the well site. No oil dirt on site, no
              dripping and leaking at oil tank and manifold system area.
       After the well is completed, reinforce the sewage pit ，solidify the disposed
          mud and have environment procedure fulfilled.
       Install fuel supply lines and keep them in good condition.
       All the drilling fluid materials shall be recovered and shall not be left at the
              well site after completion.
       The environmental protection personnel from COMPANY and operator side
                shall check and accept the well site environment according to the regulation
                after completion. Only well site environment is qualified, the well can be
               delivered.
       Transition Area for Hazardous Waste shall also be provided by each
        COMPANY in his allocated area,
       PPL/PEDEC shall approve each area before use as well. The transition area of
             hazardous waste shall be:
        Paved, fenced, marked and illuminated
        Equipped with appropriate Fire Extinguisher and other emergency response
         equipment (e.g., Eye-Wash and Emergency Shower, appropriate First Aid kits,
           neutralizer substances etc.).
        In compliance with the requirements of handling, transportation and storage of
         hazardous waste (based on usage chemical MSDS).
        Configured to accommodate a safe physical separation of incompatible waste
          materials  (e.g., acids, and alkalis, organic materials and strong oxidizing
           agents).
        Capable enough to provide storage for the entire range of hazardous wastes
          generated during the work.
       The area shall be provided with Spill Containment and means of preventing run
           off to and from the area.

        All waste containers to be stored shall be appropriately labeled.
        Hazardous Waste shall be transferred in a timely manner, within a maximum

       Standard of utilization and discharging of wastes on location
       Conduct drilling operation according to the design, drilling mud is needed
              before spud.
       Sewage that cannot be recovered shall be put into the pit， do not discharge
       Make full use of waste water. Water in mud pump and water brake must be
                utilized by circulating. Water that is used to wash drill floor, shall be recovered
                after deposition. The recovery rate of waste water shall reach 85％.
       Disposed  oil  shall be recovered  entirely. Recovery rate  shall be 100％.
           Dumping of waste oil shall be prohibited.
       In drilling operation, non-chrome thinner high temperature mud system shall be
             used often if engineering is qualified.
       While drilling in special area adopt mud creation inhabitation techniques to
              decrease the waste mud creation.
       After completion, all the mud chemicals, bentonite, clays shall be recovered
            and shall not be left at the well site. Mud in purifying tank shall also be
              recovered after completion.
       In case of any flammable or noxious gas encountered, steps shall be taken at
             once to prevent kicks and blowout. Gas shall be guided into ignition equipment
               to burn it away.
       Burning material that may result in serious smog or horrible smell at the well
                 site is not allowed. For cement or barite that may result in granular dust
               pollution, operation shall be performed in a closed system.
       For abandoned well, filled with cement plugs to seal the oil, gas or water
              formation.
       COMPANY/Generators are required to transport all generated wastes to the
                location/facilities   designated,   and   licensed  by   authorities   and/or
              approved/verified by the PPL/PEDEC (as appropriate).
       All wastes shall be transferred by approved Sub‐ COMPANY (which could be
             a 3rd party Sub-COMPANY of the COMPANY/Generator itself). The Waste
              Transporter and any other waste management service COMPANY shall be
              licensed in accordance with local regulations and are in compliance with such
               regulations. PPL/PEDEC shall verify and approve the Waste Transportation
        COMPANY by checking licenses and qualifications, audit and inspections,
               verification of human resources and received trainings etc.
       The transportation COMPANY shall ensure that all wastes are transported in a
               safe and responsible manner.

        Well Control

         1.  Installation Requirements of BOP Stack and Control System:

       The distance between BOP control lines and relief lines shall be not less than
            1m. Steel Gap Bridge should be placed in such a way to protect lines from
           damage by vehicle crossing. Sundries shall not be packed on the control line
                shield, on which welding operations are forbidden.

       The air supply shall be separated from that of driller’s console and directly
             connected to the main air supply system, and shall be equipped with liquid/gas
               separators. Excessive bending and pinching on air hoses are forbidden.

       Electric power to BOP control system shall be directly from the main switch of
               the power board, and controlled by independent switches.

       Accumulators shall be in good condition, charged at its rated value, and ready
               for work at any time.

         2. Installation Requirements of Choke Lines and Kill Lines, and Relief Lines:

            a) Beside the drilling spool, one manual and one HCR gate valves on the side of
            chock manifold and two manual gate valves on the side of kill manifold shall
             be equipped, and the manual gate valve close to the spool shall be always open.

           b) The high-pressure co-flex hose shall be installed as straight as possible and
              fixed by anchor after installation.

            c) Relief lines (burning line and bleed line):

       No field welding is permitted on relief lines and the connecting style of relief
                lines must be flanged.
       The arrangement of relief lines shall take wind directions, dwellings, roads, oil
              tank areas, power lines and other facilities into consideration.
       While the two lines go in the same trend, the distance between the lines shall
             be at least 0.3m, and the two lines shall be fixed independently.
       The outlets of bleed line connecting with choke manifold shall be in a safe area
            which is at least 300m. The bleed line on the kill manifold side connecting with
                drilling spool shall be prepared and connected when necessary (about 70m from
               the wellhead).
       At every 10m~15m, turning points, and outlets, the lines shall be supported and
              fixed by cement foundations with anchor bolts or ground anchors. Hanging

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 199 of 240053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

              portions shall be supported firmly. If crossing the stumbling blocks such as
             brooks or ponds is needed, metal bridging supports are necessary.
       Pre-buried anchor bolts for cement foundations shall not be less than 20mm or
              3/4" in diameter, and greater than 0.5m in length.

             3. Pressure test value and requirements:

            a) A pressure test shall be conducted successfully where there is no pressure
              decline in 5 minutes for a low-pressure test and a minimum of 10 minutes for a
              high-pressure test.

           b) Prior to each high-pressure test, a low-pressure test with 200-300 psi shall be
               carried out to verify sealing capability at the circumstance of low pressure and
             avoid washing out sealing elements.

            c) High pressure test should be to the rated working pressure of ram preventers or
               the rated working pressure of the wellhead, whichever is the lowest, or to the
               rating required in DRILLING ROGRAM. Variable bore rams should be
                 initially pressure tested on the largest and smallest OD pipe sizes that may be
             used during the OPERATION. Annular preventers, with a joint of drill pipe
                installed, should be tested to 70% of their working pressure. The high test for
             Kelly cocks,  kill lines and choke lines should be to their rated working
               pressures, each part in the choke manifold is tested respectively to its rated
            working pressures, the relief lines be pressure tested to no less than 1,450psi
             (10Mpa).

           d) When casing cup tester is used, the above test pressure should not exceed 80%
              of the internal yield pressure (burst pressure) of the exposed casing.

            e) The control system of BOP shall be pressure tested to 3,000psi (21Mpa) for its
                 reliability before putting into use.

              f) Except that the BOP control system is tested with hydraulic oil, other well
               control equipment shall be pressure tested by clear water.

           g) Testing tools

       All required sizes of the plug type testers, and cup type testers should be
               available for pressure testing purpose.

       When the cup type tester(s) is used for pressure test, the connection of the cup
                testers has to be checked, to ensure  it will stand the load during the high
              pressures test. For surface casing, the cup tester is to be set in middle of the first

              casing joint in the top, so the first casing connection (between wellhead and
              casing head housing) below the well head is to be tested too while testing BOP
            and wellhead.

         4. Pressure test frequency:

      All ram type preventers, annular BOP, valves, choke and kill lines, choke manifold,
     Kelly valves and safety valves should be pressure tested at the following frequencies:

       Prior to installation where possible.

       After installation of wellhead and BOP assembly and prior to drilling.

       After the disconnection or repair of any pressure containment seal in the BOP
               stack, choke line, or choke manifold, but limited to the affected component.

       Prior to drilling into a confirmed or suspected high-pressure zone.

       At any time requested by the COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE.

       In any case, every one month or during the first trip after the one-month interval
             with a maximum interval of 45 days. This frequency is not required for shear
              rams. As a minimum, the shear rams are to be tested prior to resume drilling
              operation after 9-5/8” casing string has been set and adequate WOC.

         5. Work Requirement of Well Control Equipment:

       With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1000psi, while snubbing with annular
               preventer, drill tools shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, and the snubbing
               velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

       After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing
              pressure not greater than 2000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up and down
             with the velocity less than 0.2m/s, however, rotating or tool joint passing
             through are forbidden.

       While drilling through pay zone and thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test
               for the BOPs shall be performed regularly.

       Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

       The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated
            on choke manifolds.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 201 of 240053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

       All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers,
            and be indicated with on/Off.

       In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams,
                retrieve the upper sheared drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve
                installed into the hole and close pipe rams on it to prevent the possibility of
              shear ram’s failure.

         6. Management of Well Control Equipment:

       Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed and
              operated by designated personnel with clear post responsibilities.

       Well  site shall have specified component storeroom and rubber element
             storeroom with air conditioners respectively. The temperature of storerooms
                shall meet storage requirements of components and rubber elements.

       At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well
                  site. Ram preventer side door seals and ram rubber, every type gasket and bolt
                 etc. should be enough for backup.

         7. Killing Method and Shut-in Method:

       Driller's method is recommended for well killing.

       The hard Shut-in method is recommended for shutting in the well in Fahliyan
                reservoir.

         8. Well Control during drilling:

            a) Shut in Procedure in While on Bottom
       Position Kelly (if in use) and tool joint so that tool joints are clear of sealing
              elements.
       Shut off pumps, check for flow.
       If flow is noted, close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke
                line valve (HCR).
       If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe
            rams vs. toll joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks
       Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (if possible).
       Record shut-in drill pipe and casing pressures.
       Record volume gain and mark pits.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 202 of 240053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

       Weigh mud in suction pits.
       Check blowout preventer and manifold for leaks.
       Check flowline and choke exhaust for flow.
       Check accumulator pressure.

           b) Shut in Procedure in While Tripping
       If a flow is detected, install full opening safety valve and close same.
       Position tool joints clear of the sealing elements and close annular preventer
            and open remote-controlled choke line valve (HCR).
       Make up grey valve (dart type inside BOP on full open safety valve). Then
          Make up Kelly or top drive (insert a pup joint or single between safety valve
            and top drive) and open safety valve.
       Record casing pressure.
       Check blowout preventer, stack, and manifold for leaks.
       Check valves for correct position.
       Check accumulator pressure.
       Begin stripping to bottom.

            c) Shut in Procedure for Empty Wells
       Try to RIH with drill pipe as more as possible if hole condition permits, and the
                  drill pipe must be installed a Kelly cock or safety valve.
       Close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke line valve
            (HCR).
       If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe
            rams vs. tool joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks
       Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (jf possible).
       Record casing pressure

         9. Well Control During Running Casing:

     The well control while running casing is important and critical, best practices shall be
      followed, including but not limited to:
       Change out pipe rams to casing rams prior to running casing into hydrocarbon
              bearing formation, if possible.
       The crossover between casing and drill pipe has to be available, and good
               practice is to make it up with a joint of DP and keep on V-door.

        10. Shut in Procedure During Logging:

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 203 of 240053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

     Cable shall be pull out of the hole immediately when overflow is found during logging.
       If pit gain exceeds the specified amount, the cable shall be cut immediately and treat the
     overflow in accordance with the shut-in procedure for empty wells. Continuing to pull
      the cable through the closed annular preventer is not recommended.

        11. Well Control During Testing:
       No difference to while DRILLING OPERATION, since either there is testing
                string in the well (same as Shut-in procedure while on bottom), or tripping the
                string. (Same as shut-in procedure while tripping).
       Likely there is some crude in the testing string, and precaution has to be taken
             while circulating the crude out of hole during killing operations to ensure it is
              properly handled without causing environmental impact.
       To minimize the formation damage, the killing fluids used shall be weighted
              brine if possible, however in well control case when it occurs, killing well safely
               will take priority rather than protecting formation from damage on selection of
                killing fluids.

        12. Well Control During Stimulation:
       Similar to during testing.
       For any residual or alive acid to be circulated out during killing operations,
             measures have to be taken to treat the returned acid properly to avoid personnel
            from getting hurt, and without causing any environmental damage.

        13. Well Control Drills:

      Drills shall be conducted only when hole conditions and other rig activities permit. Drills
     should be scheduled so that crews can practice drills while on bottom, while tripping in
     and while out of the hole. Each operating shift shall perform at least one BOP drill under
      different situations per month.

        14. Basic Requirement of Well Control:
       For 13-5/8”, 10K BOP, BOP should be schemed as follows: upper rams 5”,
             middle rams are shear rams, lower rams is variable rams (2-7/8” to 5”). For
               easily connecting, armored fire-resistant 10000psi and ID 4-1/16" flexible
             hoses are recommended as kill/choke lines which connected with BOP directly.
       The BOP stack and choke manifold, kill line and choke line, HCR and manual
              gate valves, inside BOP (including kelly cock) have to be H2S trimmed and
              stand the working temperature from -10 degrees C (in case of doing N2 for

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title

                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 204 of 240053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0027      00

           DST) to the maximum up to 100 deg C (estimated highest temperature
               condition).
       The BOP  equipment  shall  be  visually  inspected,  function  tested, and
               hydrostatically pressure  tested during commissioning and Acceptance of
               Drilling Unit prior to Commencement Date, then upon installation on a
              wellhead, prior to drilling any hole section with a potential hydrocarbon bearing
                reservoir, after breaking any BOP connection (such as after installation of an
               additional wellhead section after running casing), and at least every 14-21 days
             while the BOP is installed on the Well.
       CONTRACTOR shall submit the current well control procedures manual of
         CONTRACTOR to COMPANY for review and approval by COMPANY.
             Valid IWCF Well Control Certificates (or IADC equivalent) must be held by
                  all tool pushers, Drillers (optional) at Drilling Supervisor level and Drillers and
               Assistant Drillers at Driller level, as further specified in CONTRACTOR
              Personnel HSE Requirements.
       The accumulator must be of sufficient capacity so that it is possible to close one
               (1) ram and the bag, open a ram and the bag, re-close a ram and the bag and
                retain 1200psi accumulator pressure.
       The “OPEN” and “CLOSED” operating positions of BOP activators of the
              rams, annular, and remote actuated valves must be clearly identified on the BOP
             master control panel and remote panels, in English in addition to the native
             language of the majority of the senior drilling crew.
       Shear-ram BOP activator must have a flap-cover to ensure only pre-meditated
            and deliberated activation and to prevent accidental WORK.
       All lines and connections in the choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold,
            choke and kill lines and high-pressure mud lines should be welded hard-piping
             with weld-on FMC Weco “hammer-lug” 1502 unions (or Western equivalent,
             such as Anson) or weld-on API flanges. The well control system should not
              include any threaded screw-on hammer-lug unions, flanges, or other threaded
             screw-on connections.
       All  adapter or spacer spools between  the wellhead and BOP must be
             manufactured in accordance with API 6A, and must be complete with all
              required studs, nuts, and ring gasket seals for both lower and upper connections;
           minimum spare parts should include two (2) OEM spare studs complete with
              nuts and two spare OEM ring gasket seals for both bottom and top connections.
       There should be a wide-bore gas vent line from the “poor-boy” degasser; the
                line and line outlet must be securely anchored, the line outlet must be a safe
              distance from the well cellar, rig floor, choke manifold, and mud logging unit.

       Well Control Equipment Welding: All welds in the well control system must
             be NDT inspected and records maintained of all welding and weld inspections,
              including choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold, mud pump discharge
              manifold, choke and kill lines.
       Well Control Rig Floor Information: The following must be posted on the rig
               floor (in the Driller’s shack  / “dog-house”): Well Shut-In Procedure, Well
              Information Sheet (showing casing and hole sizes, depths, and such like), Kill
             Sheet (including most recent slow circulation rate pressures, formation integrity
               leak-off test information and MAASP, present mud weight, present drill string
            and well volumes, and such like).
       The derrick substructure clear height (rotary table to ground level) needs to be
            enough for fitting in above BOP configuration (including a tubing head and a
                bell nipple). This need to be double checked in rig tender process. According to
               the calculation of height of BOP stack, the substructure clear height is at least
            9 m.
       In the case if drilling 6-1/8" hole becomes necessary, or using 3-1/2" drill pipe
               for the cleanup run (including drill 7" shoe track), then taper drilling string (5"
         DP + 3-1/2" DP) is to be run, so a pair variable ram be installed in the single
           ram preventer. The defect installing variable ram in single ram preventer is that
               the ram may be damaged and the string fall in hole bottom due to the ram
             hanging up too much weight when the drill pipe be cut. If the pipe ram be
                installed in the single ram preventer and the variable ram be installed in the
             double ram preventer, it would be very dangerous due to the variable ram failure
               in frequently using.

       H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure

    As per PPL/PEDEC SOW South Azadegan oilfield contains H2S bearing formations,
      precautions shall be taken in place especially in 12-1/4” & 8-1/2” hole section (for
      typical Fahliyan vertical well) while drilling, completion and well testing operation.
    H2S can be released any time while drilling, completion and well testing operation,
      therefore:
       The Rig shall be prepared for H2S (Training, procedures and protective gear).
       Make sure everyone on the Rig should be made aware of the hazard presented
              by H2S during their induction when they first arrive on the rig.
       The mud shall be treated to protect the drill pipe and the casing.
       All training program shall be recorded and reported.

       Adequate sensors and alarms must be installed for the scope of monitoring
